newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 6.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former parliament president Ukrit Mongkolnavin's quest for the chairmanship of the Constitution Drafting Assembly has run into strong opposition from democracy groups, which oppose him for his alleged past services to a dictatorial regime. Core leaders of 19 pro-democracy organisations forming a pressure group to campaign for constitutional reform say they cannot accept Ukrit because of his alleged past links with dictatorship. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Police will request an arrest warrant next week for former deputy interior minister Suchart Tancharoen over his alleged involvement with land grabbing scam in Nong Khai province. The warrant's issuance has yet to be formally agreed upon by an investigative team in charge of the case. (THE NATION)

- Leaders of community groups across Thailand have called for an end to government intervention in the media. They say the government has cancelled several environment and politics-related radio programmes, especially those allowing listeners to call in to air their opinions. (BANGKOK POST)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh is mobilising support to expand Don Muang International Airport's capacity through the relocation of the adjacent Air Force base rather than speed up work on a new international airport at Nong Ngu Hao. During the Banharn Silpa-archa government, Chavalit, in his capacity as deputy prime minister, headed the Second Bangkok International Airport Development Project Committee, but failed to push through an action plan that would complete the Nong Ngu Hao airport on schedule. (THE NATION)

- The government has outlined measures to help the ailing property sector which may include a controversial scheme to take over bad loans from banks and finance companies, says central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond. Most controversial will be the plan to set up a find similar to the U.S. Resolution Trust to take over bad loans from banks and finance companies for resale. (BUSINESS DAY)
